title: PyTorch: Autograd & Computation Graph
subtitle: Dynamic DAG, requires_grad & .backward() Flow
summary: Trace forward tensor operations and reverse-mode .backward() gradient flow across nn.Module.

evaluationChart.title: Autograd Training Loss per Step
evaluationChart.description: Tracks loss reduction as .backward() accumulates gradients and optimizer.step() updates weights.

advantages: Define-by-run dynamic computation graph works natively with Python control flow.
Automatic reverse-mode differentiation (.backward()) computes exact gradients in one pass.
Seamless CUDA / Apple MPS GPU acceleration via .to(device).
limitations: Forgetting optimizer.zero_grad() silently accumulates gradients across batches.
Keeping graphs in memory without torch.no_grad() during eval causes OOM.
Dynamic Python dispatch overhead unless compiled with torch.compile().

codeTemplates.pytorch:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

x = torch.tensor([[2.0, 1.0]])
y = torch.tensor([[5.0]])
model = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2, 4), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(4, 1))
opt = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.05)

loss = nn.MSELoss()(model(x), y)
opt.zero_grad()
loss.backward()  # Populates .grad
opt.step()
print('Loss:', loss.item())
